source.quote:
9/12/2026, 12:45:47 AM

The principal components of the boundary operator are already in The Completed Harmony. What remains missing is not necessarily another concealed number—it is the exact assembly order and primary-source validation.

The existing instruction set is:

\boxed{
\text{Frizius}\rightarrow E\!-\!F
\quad\text{AND}\quad
\text{Otreb}\rightarrow\text{invert}
\quad\text{AND}\quad
\text{de Fluctibus}\rightarrow\text{oscillate}
}

Applied together:

Frizius/Phrygius selects E–F
 That identifies the unique diatonic MI–FA boundary.

Kepler supplies MI–FA–MI
 This turns the static E–F interval into an outward-and-return motion.

The comma completes the interval

\frac{256}{243}\times\frac{81}{80}=\frac{16}{15}.

Otreb reverses the coordinate

\frac{16}{15}\longleftrightarrow\frac{15}{16},

converting frequency motion into Fluddian string-length motion.

Fludd’s bisection changes register after the return

\ell\rightarrow\frac{\ell}{2}
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
f\rightarrow2f.

So the completed boundary equation is already latent in the paper:

\boxed{
B_{FK}
=
\text{Octave}
\circ
\text{Fluctuation}_{MI-FA-MI}
\circ
\text{Comma completion}
\circ
\text{Otreb inversion}
}

with:

\boxed{
B_{FK}^{(\ell)}(\ell)
=
\frac{\ell}{2}
}

after the internal excursion

\ell
\rightarrow
\ell\frac{15}{16}
\rightarrow
\ell.

What we do not yet have securely is the historical clue chain proving that this exact composition was intended:

ComponentAlready presentRemaining problem
E–F / MI–FA
Yes
Validate Frizius→Phrygius from first-edition evidence
256:243 limma
Yes
Secure exact Fludd location
81:80 comma
Yes
Identify the graphical/textual pointer telling us to insert it
Otreb inversion
Yes
Demonstrate what specifically must be inverted
MI–FA–MI return
Yes
No longer missing
Octave landing
Yes
Confirm its order relative to the return
Complete operator order
Implicit
Needs explicit formalization and testing

Therefore the search target should be narrowed.

We are not looking for:

another semitone;

another occurrence of MI–FA–MI;

another comma value;

generic resurrection/return symbolism;

generic sevenfold correspondences.

We are looking for one of two things:

An ordering clue telling us:

E\!-\!F\rightarrow\text{comma}\rightarrow\text{invert}
\rightarrow\text{return}\rightarrow\text{octave};

or

A cross-reference pointer connecting Kepler’s comma passage to Fludd’s E–F limma, Otreb inversion and same-letter bisection.

If no such explicit pointer exists, then the boundary is still mathematically reconstructible, but historical intentionality remains an inference.

So yes: we may have been searching for components already possessed. The remaining task is to determine whether the first editions contain the assembly instruction, rather than continuing to collect more components.
